head: Menu translator app BADè reads menus and signs on your photo
dek: BADè is a new $9.99 iPhone app for travelers that shows the translation of a menu, street sign or pharmacy label right on the photo you take. It was #83 in Travel on the US App Store's paid chart on 17 November, a day after it came out.
details: For menus it shows each dish's original text, translation, how to say it, a plain explanation and the price, and points out allergens and warnings. You can also type or speak a phrase to hear it translated, save phrases in a phrasebook and show one full screen to someone. The maker says it detects more than 30 languages, including Japanese, Korean, Chinese and Arabic. It has no account, no in-app purchases and no tracking, and scans are kept on the phone.
where: iPhone and iPad, $9.99 one-time on the App Store (out since 16 November)
means: If you travel where you can't read the menu, this translates it on the photo and flags allergens, for a one-time price with no subscription.
todo: Make sure the language of your next trip is covered before buying; the listing names some of them.
